title: Heuristic Reflective Chain-of-Thought: Enhancing Multi-Step Reasoning in Large Language Models With  Reflection and Heuristic Guidance

items.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
items.abstract: Arabic Large Language Models exhibit a pronounced deficit in multi-stepreasoning, mathematical problem-solving, and agentic planning relative to their En-glish counterparts - a gap we attribute to the scarcity of high-quality Arabic chain-of-thought (CoT) training data and suboptimal tokenization of Arabic script. Wepresent AraCoT-Agent, a rigorous framework for distilling structured reasoning ca-pabilities from frontier teacher models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B) into smaller, de-ployable Arabic-focused models via reward-weighted supervised fine-tuning. Cen-tral to our approach is AraCoT, the first curated, quality-filtered Arabic reason-ing trace dataset constructed through a five-stage filtering pipeline that enforces an-swer correctness (ε ≤ 10−3), fluency bounds via AraBERT perplexity, structuralcompleteness, and near-duplicate removal using MinHash-based Jaccard similarity.We formalize the training objective as a GRPO-style reward-weighted cross-entropyloss with composite reward r(x, c) = λ1 · 1[correct] + λ2 · |c|/Lmax + λ3 · fluency(c),which down-weights gradients for already high-quality examples. We further intro-duce AraAgent-Bench, a 500-problem benchmark spanning five agentic reasoningtask types across five difficulty tiers, with formal difficulty defined by minimum solu-tion steps. Through controlled experiments comparing QLoRA fine-tuning (rank 64,4-bit NF4) on Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B against full fine-tuning on Qwen3-4B,we demonstrate that our best model achieves a 55.7% relative improvement over thestrongest baseline (Llama3-8B base, 30.0%) on AraAgent-Bench ((46.7-30.0)/30.0 ×100; p < 0.05, McNemar’s test), substantially closing the Arabic-English reasoninggap. Ablation studies reveal that data quality dominates quantity, GRPO weightingyields consistent gains over standard SFT, and tokenization efficiency (ρQwen ≈ 1.8vs. ρLlama ≈ 3.2 tokens per Arabic word) is a significant predictor of cross-lingualreasoning transfer.
